Day 1
From Hotel: 14 min → Fortaleza do Monte & Macau Museum
1.Fortaleza do Monte & Macau Museum
Built by the Jesuits between 1617 and 1626 on a 52-metre hill, this fort still carries 32 muzzle-loading cannon along its walls and gives a 360° view over the peninsula; the Macau Museum inside covers four centuries of the city's history.
Read more

Closed Monday
Fort grounds stay open 7:00am - 7:00pm, beyond the museum's own hours.
~1 hr

9 min · 7 min → Ruins of St. Paul's
2.Ruins of St. Paul's
The granite façade and grand staircase are all that survive of a Jesuit church built in 1602–1640 and gutted by fire in 1835 — five tiers of carving blending Christian, Chinese and Japanese imagery, once acclaimed as the "Vatican of the Far East."
Read more

~30 min

3.Lou Kau Mansion
The 1889 courtyard home of merchant Lou Kau, blending Chinese blue-brick construction with Portuguese decorative touches — three courtyards, carved friezes and oyster-shell windows, restored and opened to the public in 2005.

4.Guia Fortress · Chapel & Lighthouse
A 17th-century fort crowning Macau's highest hill at 91.6 metres, with a whitewashed 1865 lighthouse — the oldest Western-style lighthouse on the China coast — and a chapel frescoed with fused Chinese-and-Christian imagery. A free cable car climbs the hill from Flora Garden.

Day 2
From Hotel: 9 min → Mandarin's House
1.Mandarin's House
The childhood home of Qing-dynasty reformist Zheng Guanying, begun in 1869 by his father — more than 60 rooms across several courtyards, mixing Lingnan brick-and-timber construction with Portuguese shutters and stucco, restored and reopened in 2010.
Read more
Thursday - Tuesday 10:00am - 6:00pm
Closed Wednesday
~45 min
Free
10 Travessa de António da Silva · São Lourenço
8 min · 2 min → A-Ma Temple
2.A-Ma Temple
Built in 1488 to honour Mazu, the sea goddess, this is Macau's oldest temple and the source of the city's name — Portuguese sailors misheard "A-Ma-Gau" as "Macau." Six pavilions climb the rock face, mixing Taoist, Buddhist and folk worship.
Read more
Daily 7:00am - 6:00pm
~45 min
Free
Largo da Barra · Barra
11 min · 3 min → Macau Tower
3.Macau Tower
A 338-metre tower designed by Gordon Moller, opened in 2001, with a glass-floor Skywalk around the rim of the 58th-floor observation deck and the world's highest commercial bungy jump at 233 metres — a hard pivot from the historic centre to modern Macau.
Read more

18 min · 4 min → Senado Square
4.Senado Square
A 3,700-square-metre plaza paved in a black-and-white Portuguese wave pattern, enclosed by the Leal Senado, the General Post Office and the Holy House of Mercy — the civic centre of Macau since the 16th century and the start of the Historic Centre's walking route.
Read more
Open 24/7
~30 min

1.Taipa Houses-Museum
Five mint-green colonial villas built in 1921 for well-off Portuguese families, restored as period rooms, a Macanese living-heritage exhibit and a creative-arts space — one of the "Eight Views of Macau" on the old Taipa waterfront.

11 min → Chapel of St. Francis Xavier
2.Chapel of St. Francis Xavier
A yellow 1928 Baroque chapel facing a small square in Coloane Village, built to hold relics of St. Francis Xavier and of Catholic martyrs crucified in Nagasaki in 1597 — the relics have since moved to the crypt behind the Ruins of St. Paul's.
Read more

3.Macao Giant Panda Pavilion
A fan-shaped, 3,000-square-metre pavilion in Seac Pai Van Park holding Macau's resident giant pandas — Kai Kai, Xin Xin and their twin cubs — alongside gibbons, flamingos and other rescued animals in a wooded corner of Coloane.

Macau's largest natural beach, a 1,350-metre curve on Coloane's southern shore named for the dark, glauconite-flecked sand along its waterline — a quiet, unhurried close to the itinerary, with beach shacks serving Portuguese-style grilled food along the promenade.

Local Tastes
Portuguese Egg Tart
Custard tart with a crisp, flaky shell and a slightly caramelized, wobbly filling. Invented in 1989 by Englishman Andrew Stow at his Coloane bakery — now Macau's signature pastry, sold hot from the oven.
Lord Stow's Bakery · Margaret's Café e Nata
Pork Chop Bun
A bone-in pork chop, marinated and deep-fried, tucked whole into a crusty Portuguese-style bun. Born from Portuguese colonial café culture in old Taipa, with no sauce needed beyond the meat's own char.
Tai Lei Loi Kei · Sei Kee Café
Almond Cookies
Charcoal-fired almond shortbread cookies, pressed and baked fresh on the spot at street-facing ovens. Macau's most popular edible souvenir, sold warm in paper-wrapped stacks along the food streets.
Koi Kei Bakery · Pastelaria Fong Kei
African Chicken
Chicken baked in a rich sauce of peanuts, coconut, tomato and chili — a Macanese chef's 1940s invention using spices brought back from Portugal's African colonies. The dish that defines Macanese fusion cooking.
Restaurante Litoral · Riquexó
Serradura
Layers of whipped cream and finely crushed Marie biscuit crumbs, chilled into a light, no-bake dessert. The crumbs resemble sawdust — serradura in Portuguese — a simple Macanese café staple found across the city.
Gelatina Mok Yei Kei
Food Delivery
mFood
Foreign number: not accepted. — SMS verification requires a Macao, Hong Kong, or Mainland Chinese mobile number; a foreign number cannot complete signup.
The largest delivery network in Macau by restaurant count, with some orders arriving in under 15 minutes. The interface is only partly translated to English, and foreign bank cards are widely reported to fail at checkout.
mfoodapp.com
Aomi
Foreign number: not accepted. — SMS verification requires a Macao, Hong Kong, or Mainland Chinese mobile number; a foreign number cannot complete signup.
A broader lifestyle app that bundles food delivery with taxi-hailing, hotel booking, and group-buy deals — useful if you need more than a meal, but the ordering flow sits under everything else the app offers.
aomi.mo
TikBee
Foreign number: not accepted. — SMS verification requires a Macao, Hong Kong, or Mainland Chinese mobile number; a foreign number cannot complete signup.
Bundles restaurant delivery with supermarket and department-store orders under one app. Best known on Taipa Island and around the ZAPE district — check restaurant coverage near your address before relying on it.
tikbee.com

Getting Around
Uber
Foreign number: accepted. — the code comes by SMS to any international number, on the same global Uber account used everywhere else.
Relaunched in Macau as a taxi-booking and payment platform, not a private ride service — it books and pays for a licensed Macau taxi at the official meter fare. Multi-language interface, no cash needed, and the same app works for the Hong Kong cross-border limousine service.
uber.com
Train Stations Near Hotel
Hengqin Railway Station
Zhuhai–Zhuhai Airport intercity rail, connecting into China's national high-speed network → Guangzhou · Shenzhen · Zhuhai Airport. Macau has no railway of its own — this is the closest station of any kind, reached by crossing into Zhuhai.
Board the Macau LRT Hengqin line at Lotus Station — a 2-minute cross-border shuttle straight into the Hengqin Port terminal, which adjoins the railway station on the Zhuhai side.
Hengqin Railway Station · Hengqin · Zhuhai
20 min · 4 min → hotel
Day Trips by Train
Zhuhai · 30 min
A relaxing coastal city just across the border, with a scenic waterfront promenade, offshore islands, and the giant Fisher Girl statue on Xianglu Bay. A slower-paced contrast to Macau's casino resorts, built around seafood and sea views.
book at: 12306
Jiangmen · 1h 30min
Home to the UNESCO-listed Kaiping Diaolou — fortified watchtowers built in the 1920s by Chinese emigrants returning to their home villages after making fortunes abroad, blending Roman domes, Gothic arches and Chinese tiled roofs. Zili Village holds the best-preserved cluster, set among rice fields and countryside.
book at: 12306
Guangzhou · 1h 45min
Guangdong's provincial capital and one of China's oldest trading ports. The Chen Clan Ancestral Hall is the finest surviving Lingnan-style temple complex in the country, and Shamian Island's tree-lined streets preserve its 19th-century foreign-concession architecture.
book at: 12306
Shenzhen · 2h 15min
China's tech capital, a fishing village turned megacity in a single generation. The Shenzhen Museum and the OCT-LOFT creative district anchor a day built around modern China rather than Macau's colonial-era streets.
book at: 12306

Heads Up
Casinos — Minimum Age Is 21
Macau's gambling age is 21, not 18 — ID is checked at every casino floor entrance, even when just passing through to a restaurant.
MacauSoul — Unpredictable Hours
This Rua de São Paulo wine bar sometimes shuts for weeks with no notice — call or check social media before the walk over.
Hengqin Border Crossing — Bring a Passport
The LRT shuttle into Zhuhai takes 2 minutes, but immigration still requires a passport and exit/entry stamps on both sides.

Worth Knowing

Four Centuries of Portugal, Still on the Table

Macau was a Portuguese trading post from 1557 until the 1999 handover — nearly 450 years, the longest European colonial presence in Asia. That history is why the calçada wave-pattern paving under Senado Square's fountain is the same Portuguese cobblestone found in Lisbon, why street signs still carry Portuguese names above their Chinese translations, and why a food scene built on Cantonese technique also produced African Chicken and the Portuguese egg tart — dishes that exist nowhere else in China.

The casino skyline tells a newer, faster version of the same story. Macau overtook Las Vegas in gaming revenue in 2006 and now earns several times more — a single territory smaller than Manhattan, built almost entirely on land reclaimed from the sea between the old Portuguese town and the islands of Taipa and Coloane, generating more gambling revenue than any other place on Earth.
